From repo root: cd frontend && npm install && npm run build (MUST precede pip install; pyproject bundles frontend/dist as package-data). Then cd .. && python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install . — no real key is needed just to boot: export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-placeholder. # What this repository is

Companion repository for the CHI 2025 paper "Plan-Then-Execute: An Empirical
Study of User Trust and Team Performance When Using LLM Agents As A Daily
Assistant." It has two parts: `interface/` is the Flask study interface
248 participants used (a plan-then-execute LLM agent for daily-assistant
tasks like booking flights or paying bills), and `data_analysis/` is a set
of Jupyter notebooks over the anonymized study data that produce the
paper's figures and statistics.

## 1. Run the study interface (the app itself)

```
bash .engelbart/start.sh
```

Starts the Flask app (`gunicorn wsgi:app`) on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Ready
within ~5 seconds. Open in a browser:

```
http://127.0.0.1:8000/planning_agent/user_port?PROLIFIC_PID=demo
```

This is the actual entry point participants used (normally reached via a
Prolific recruitment link that appends `PROLIFIC_PID`); it sets up a session
and redirects to the consent form, then the task flow. `/hello` is a trivial
health-check route with no DB/session dependency.

**What was changed to make it boot, and why:**

- `interface/flaskr/db.py` hardcoded `postgresql+psycopg2://` with an empty
  host (`internal_link = ""`), which only ever worked on Render where a
  Postgres add-on is already running. No Postgres server exists in this
  sandbox and none can be installed system-wide (no `sudo`, no `apt` access,
  no Docker). Since this is a "no Postgres available" gap rather than an
  external secret, `db.py` now:
  - uses `DATABASE_URL` if you set it (e.g. pointing at a real Postgres
    instance you provision), otherwise
  - falls back to a self-contained, embedded Postgres server via the
    `pgserver` PyPI package (added to `requirements_new.txt`), which runs
    entirely as your own user with no root and no system service. Data
    lives in `.engelbart/data/pgdata/` (gitignored) and the server starts
    and stops with the app process.
  - `pgserver` also needed `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` pointed at a writable path
    (the sandbox's `/run/user/<uid>` is not writable); `db.py` now always
    sets it to `.engelbart/data/xdg_runtime/` before importing `pgserver`.
- `interface/flaskr/db.py` only creates tables via the `flask init-db` CLI
  command (not automatically on app start) — this was already true of the
  original code but is easy to miss since `interface/README.md` never
  mentions it (only `interface/run.sh` does). `.engelbart/start.sh` and
  `.engelbart/check.sh` both run `flask init-db` before serving/testing.
- `SECRET_KEY` was already hardcoded to `'dev'` in `flaskr/__init__.py`, so
  it did not block boot — left as-is since changing it isn't required to
  run the app locally.

**Needs credentials for the LLM-agent features, but not for boot:**
`OPENAI_API_KEY` is read lazily (only inside `get_llm()` in
`flaskr/planning_agent.py`, when a participant actually reaches a planning
task) via `langchain-openai`'s `ChatOpenAI`. Without it, the consent form,
instructions, questionnaires,

brief.purpose: A JupyterLab 3 extension ('jupyterlab-comments', adapted here as the 'Data Analysis Assistant Interface') that adds an in-notebook commenting/suggestion side-panel with two modes—Analyst Mode (view AI-style suggestions) and Wizard Mode (an experimenter writes/toggles suggestions saved to a comment file that the analyst view polls). It is the study apparatus for the CHI 2024 paper 'How Do Data Analysts Respond to AI Assistance? A Wizard-of-Oz Study' (Gu, Grunde-McLaughlin, McNutt, Heer, Althoff).
